core_obligations: Define the map by the bilinear assignment on pairs and obtain f from the universal property of the tensor product (proof lines 2316-2320).
Show surjectivity by writing every tensor as one over a common denominator tensored with a single element (proof lines 2321-2331).
Show injectivity: if the image of one over s tensor m vanishes then some t in S annihilates m, and then the tensor is rewritten as one over st tensor tm and dies (proof lines 2331-2337).
proof_roadmap: Build the canonical map from a bilinear pairing (proof lines 2315-2320).
Reduce both surjectivity and injectivity to the shape one over s tensor m (proof lines 2321-2338).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the localisation of a module is canonically isomorphic to the tensor product of the ring of fractions with it, with the isomorphism given on pure tensors by (a/s) tensor m going to am/s (statement lines 2304-2313). The proof does not invoke flatness or adjunction: it builds the map from a bilinear pairing via the universal property, reduces every tensor to the shape one over s tensor m by putting the summands over a common denominator, and proves injectivity by exhibiting an element of the multiplicative subset that annihilates the relevant numerator (proof lines 2315-2338). Reducing a general tensor to a single common denominator is the step that makes both checks possible. H2.
